description:
About the team

Trusted Access helps eligible customers access and use advanced AI capabilities with appropriate safeguards. Within User Safety & Risk Operations, we connect customer onboarding, eligibility review, access provisioning, and support into a service customers can navigate with confidence.

We work with Product, Engineering, technical support, regional operations, and customer-facing teams to resolve difficult access problems and improve the systems behind them. Our work combines sound judgment on individual cases with better products, clearer guidance, and automation that reduces unnecessary friction.

About the role

We’re looking for a senior operator to own and improve the customer access workflow for an assigned Trusted Access program. You will connect application and eligibility review, approvals, appeals, provisioning coordination, and support so customers can reach a clear, reliable outcome.

Your primary focus will be improving how the program works. You’ll use complex customer cases to uncover recurring problems, then deliver product, automation, self-service, and support-process improvements. You’ll also own difficult eligibility and access escalations, helping customers and account teams understand what is blocking progress and driving the right partners toward resolution.

This role combines independent workflow ownership with hands-on operational judgment. Success means customers reach usable access with fewer avoidable delays, decisions remain accurate, and the workflow runs reliably through the people and systems you enable.

In this role, you will:

title: Electrical Test Engineer

The Anduril Battlespace Awareness Radar team develops state-of-the-art radar systems, deployed to tackle the most significant security challenges of America and its allies. The Radar team is responsible for all aspects of radar system development, from the ideation stage through initial production.  In this role, you will work closely with an interdisciplinary technical team to perform testing and collaborate with design engineers to mature the prototypes into products. 

WHAT YOU’LL DO

• Conduct integration and developmental testing of complex electrical subystems, including high speed digital and RF components.

• Work closely with other electrical, mechanical, software, firmware, and test engineers to deliver fully functional products.

• Conduct environmental testing to ensure the reliability of our radars in various environments.

• Create and update test procedures for validating printed circuit board performance against design targets. Design test automation to streamline this testing where possible.

• Stay current with emerging technologies and industry trends to drive innovation and maintain our technological edge.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Bachelor’s Degree in Electrical Engineering or equivalent, with 3+ years of experience testing and troubleshooting complex board designs.

• Experience with analog and digital electronics testing and troubleshooting.

• Competence with test equipment such as oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, current-probes, and automation of tests.

• Familiarity with standard interfaces such as Ethernet, CAN, I2C, SPI, PCIe, USB, etc..

• Knowledge of modern analog and digital electronics and electronic circuits.

• Comfortable with a variety of electronic CAD tools (Altium preferred, Eagle and others acceptable).

• Experience with test automation scripting (e.g., Python) for data acquisition and control.

• Experience in testing and debugging for signal integrity / power integrity.

• Strong time management and organizational abilities, with a demonstrated ability to deliver projects on time and within budget.

• Excellent problem-solving skills, with the ability to think creatively and adapt to diverse and evolving challenges.

• Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

Live UI

You will apply product design and solution architecture to make security controls part of everyday work and produce reliable evidence through their operation. That evidence should support organizational excellence, audits, customers, and regulatory needs and help our audience understand and use the security information relevant to them.

You should be comfortable moving between implementation detail and consequential decisions. You'll own the power subsystem for Archimedes, end to end. You're the technical authority on everything from battery pack architecture to laser diode delivery. You set the architecture, make the calls, and stand behind your system when it goes to the range.

Your lane is deep, not wide: BMS architecture, high-voltage conversion, fault protection, and power delivery under field conditions. Our EE works alongside you on broader electrical scope. When the power system faults at a range test, you know exactly why and have a fix before the day is over.

Must-haves

- Strong experience in power electronics, with designs you've owned from schematic to field deployment

- Designed and validated 48V+ conversion and regulation systems under real operating conditions

- Set technical direction for a power subsystem as the decision-maker, without a senior engineer above you

- Hands-on wire harness design and fabrication for deployed systems, plus Altium, SPICE, and MATLAB/Simulink

- U.S. person status, required for export control

A BS or MS in Electrical Engineering, Power Electronics, or a related field, or equivalent hands-on background, is typical. What you've built matters more than where you went to school.

First 6 Months

- Architect, build, and validate the BMS for our high-voltage packs, covering safe charge and discharge, cell balancing, thermal management, and fault protection

- Design the high-voltage DC/DC conversion and diode driver electronics that deliver power to the laser

- Design and build ruggedized harnesses for the high-power laser and motor systems, from connector selection and routing to shielding and environmental protection

- Validate the power system on the range with electrical, environmental, vibration, and shock testing, and integrate it with the mechanical, optical, and robotics subsystems

- Take designs through DFM with our fabricators and into production, with schematics, BOMs, wiring diagrams, and documentation to MIL-STD and ITAR standards

Nice to Haves

- Laser diode driving or directed energy power systems

- Long-duration deployments in harsh field environments

- EMI/EMC design and shielding

- MIL-STD standards and ITAR compliance

- Background on EV powertrain, eVTOL, aerospace, or defense power teams, or Formula SAE Electric before going pro in high voltage

- An active security clearance

Not a Fit If

- You've only worked inside a large power team where someone else set the architecture

- You've only simulated and never built, tested, and debugged power hardware in the field

- You want broad electrical scope instead of deep ownership of one subsystem

- You need remote or hybrid work

How We Work

At Aurelius we work what we call, 5+X. Our core operating hours are 5 days a week, Monday to Friday, 9am to 6pm Pacific Time.

The X is the honest acknowledgment that hard work sometimes takes more. That can be late nights and weekends during sprints and ramp-up periods or conferences, deployments, and events when the mission calls for it.
This role is 5 days a week in office in San Francisco.

This role combines strategic depth and cross-organizational influence. You will work on the company's most complex initiatives, the ones that cross business units, span customer-facing and operational software, and cannot be solved inside a single team. You will work directly with executive and senior leadership to support them in defining the outcomes that matter, then break the work down across the business to expose complexity, dependencies, and risk before they slow delivery.

You define the product strategy and approach, shape the work, and bring a clear recommendation when direction is unclear. Your reach spans the entire organization, not a single team or vertical. You partner with product leads, who bring domain and product depth, and with designated business leads, who bring business ownership and context, so planning and shipping teams have clear direction and what you define gets executed well across teams.

• Work directly with senior leadership to identify target outcomes, translate business goals into clear product objectives, and define how success will be measured.

• Define the product strategy and cross-functional approach for the initiatives you support. The business owns the decisions and the outcomes, product leads and delivery teams own planning and shipping, and you own the clarity and quality of the approach that connects them.

• Break down large initiatives across business units to surface complexity, dependencies, sequencing constraints, and technical and customer experience considerations early.

• Set the approach for initiatives that scale across customer-facing and enterprise property technology, connecting the resident and associate experience to the systems and workflows behind it so decisions in one domain account for their effect on the other.

• Frame trade-off decisions, bring a clear recommendation to business leaders, and give teams the clarity to move forward once a decision is made.

• Maintain a working understanding of technical architecture and delivery constraints so you can weigh trade-offs credibly with engineering.

• Apply sound product principles to unfamiliar domains and adapt quickly to new business areas and technologies.
